Google will switch off Search in schools that turn off its AI

• Google will turn its AI tools off for K-12 students unless schools opt in, and schools that refuse AI lose Google Search too.
• Siri AI can now act inside third-party apps in a developer Preview, as Apple hints that third-party AI could bring in new revenue.
• Anthropic's quarterly revenue hit $17 billion, but compute took 58% of it, up from 48%, as it paid more for short-term capacity.

items.hook: Google says schools that switch off its AI will lose Google Search too[S1][S3].
items.text:
Google says schools that switch off its AI will lose Google Search too.

• Google plans to turn AI tools off for K-12 students unless administrators turn them on.
• There is no option to switch off the Gemini features but keep Search.
• Students in schools that block AI will see a notice that Search is not available.

Our read: Schools that rely on Google will have to accept its AI features to keep Search.

Your take: Should schools be able to keep Search without AI? Tell us in the comments.

items.hook: Anthropic now spends 58% of its revenue on compute, up from 48%[S6].
items.text:
Anthropic now spends 58% of its revenue on compute, up from 48%.

• Quarterly revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion.
• Its compute bill hit $10 billion, with $5.0 billion on pricier short-term deals.
• It has been paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for compute.

Our read: As Anthropic heads for an IPO, its margins are getting worse, not better.

Your take: Is the AI boom worth what it costs? Tell us in the comments.

items.hook: Apple is letting Siri AI carry out tasks inside third-party apps[S5].
items.text:
Apple is letting Siri AI carry out tasks inside third-party apps.

• Developers can build Siri AI's new features into all apps with iOS 27.3.
• A new app skills feature combines several tasks into a single action.
• Apple's finance chief says there are opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships.

Our read: Expect your apps to start offering Siri AI actions, starting with a developer Preview.

Your take: Would you let Siri act inside your apps? Tell us in the comments.
